title: Risk & returns around FOMC press conferences: a novel perspective from computer vision

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper constructs a novel attention measure using computer vision algorithms on video recordings of FOMC press conference Q&A sessions. By tracking facial landmarks to calculate the Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR) and measuring the time the Fed Chair spends looking down at internal documents, the author quantifies discussion complexity. This attention measure is then tested in univariate linear regressions to explain contemporaneous stock returns and the change in realized volatility around press conferences.
extraction.data_period: April 2011 to September 2020, 1-min frequency for S&P 500
extraction.universe: S&P 500 index around FOMC press conferences

key_findings: Complex discussions during FOMC press conference Q&A sessions (measured by the Fed Chair reading internal documents more frequently) are associated with higher contemporaneous equity returns.
Complex discussions lead to a drop in realized volatility, indicating uncertainty resolution.
The video-based attention measure (Delta lambda) outperforms benchmark variables like speech duration and question counts in explaining stock returns and volatility changes around press conferences.
The information revealed during Q&A sessions is incorporated immediately into stock prices and is not redundant with pre-written opening statements.
limitations: The methodology relies on the spontaneity of questions and answers; if speakers received questions in advance, the method would not work.
Excludes the FOMC conference of March 15, 2020, because only audio was available.
